name: General Post Office, Murree
assumptions: Footprint taken from the restoration plan on the board in the building (photo DSC_0347) and scaled by the OSM way 406084294 (60 m long), which contains the GPO node; the dossier found no way tagged as the GPO, so assigning it is an inference.
Plan scale 0.093 m per board pixel; the gable width of 7.6 m comes from that and a door width assumed at 2.2 m.
Heading 298 degrees (front north-west) inferred from OSM, the road alignment and the board plan's road layout; no source states it.
Main gable apex 12.8 m and eave 8.1 m measured from the front photos with a 2.2 m door as scale; no published height exists.
Wing eave 6.8 m and ridge 10 m measured from DSC_0402 only.
Terrace, retaining wall and the 2.6 m flight are estimated; about 13 risers are visible in the photos and the road level is a guess.
No photo shows the rear or the far south-west end: rear walls, rear windows and block C are built plainly from the plan, block C's height and hipped roof are guesses.
Rear toilet annexes from the plan, heights and roofs guessed.
North-east wing end drawn as a hipped roof from the slanted edge in DSC_0402 only; main gable roof covering assumed to be the same red as the wings, which is the only roof colour seen.
Right wing window and pier rhythm beyond the first bay is extrapolated from the left wing; trees hide it in every photo.
Colours sampled from DSC_0402 in strong sun and adjusted by eye; lattice and stone coursing are tile textures, not geometry; lettering, emblem and signage are left out.
Night lighting: no source; windows carry a faint glow only.
